examples.name: SARSA vs Q-Learning Cliff
examples.description: Tabular SARSA and Q-learning on a cliff grid: on-policy stays inland, off-policy hugs the rim
examples.learningGoal: See why on-policy SARSA avoids the cliff that off-policy Q-learning hugs.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints two greedy policies; Q-learning hugs the cliff and SARSA stays inland.

examples.name: Chain Rule
examples.description: Check d/dx [f(g(x))] = f'(g(x)) * g'(x) against a numerical slope — the product backprop uses
examples.learningGoal: See why backprop multiplies local derivatives before training the XOR net.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints numeric vs analytic derivatives for (2x+1)^3 and a small finite-difference error.

examples.name: Perceptron
examples.description: One neuron with a step activation: AND and OR work, XOR does not
examples.learningGoal: See a single neuron separate AND/OR, then fail on XOR before the hidden layer.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints AND/OR accuracy 4/4 and XOR below 4, then perceptron ok.

examples.name: XOR Neural Net
examples.description: Train a 2-4-1 multilayer perceptron on XOR with backpropagation, from scratch
examples.learningGoal: Read each backprop multiply as the chain-rule product from chain_rule.malda, then watch XOR train.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints the chain-rule equations, a first-sample walkthrough, training loss, and classifies all four XOR inputs correctly.

examples.name: Softmax Classifier
examples.description: Linear softmax + cross-entropy on three 2D blobs using math.matmul
examples.learningGoal: Train a 3-class softmax on 2D points after the XOR MLP.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints accuracy at least 30/36 and softmax classifier ok.

examples.name: Linear SVM
examples.description: Train a soft-margin support vector machine with hinge loss and L2, from scratch
examples.learningGoal: See a max-margin linear separator, then why the same model cannot solve XOR.
examples.expectedOutput: Separates two 2D clusters and reports that linear SVM fails on XOR.

examples.name: Attention Is All You Need
examples.description: Vaswani et al. 2017 Transformer: scaled dot-product attention, multi-head, sinusoidal PE, encoder-decoder, then a tiny reverse trainer
examples.learningGoal: Read the 2017 paper's equations as running MALDA, then watch a single attention head learn to reverse a sequence.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints paper-section walkthroughs, a learned anti-diagonal attention map, and reverse-sequence accuracy.

examples.name: microgpt (Karpathy Port)
examples.description: Pure MALDA port of Karpathy's dependency-free microgpt training and inference loop
examples.learningGoal: Train a tiny decoder-only GPT after the 2017 encoder-decoder walkthrough.
examples.expectedOutput: Runs an advanced MALDA implementation of a GPT-style training and inference loop.

examples.name: Embedding 2D
examples.description: Project hash embeddings onto two axes and list VectorDB neighbors — no GGUF required
examples.learningGoal: See why nearby words sit close after a 2D projection of hash embeddings.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints a 2D table and nearest neighbors for 'car', then embedding 2d ok.

examples.name: ONNX Inspect
examples.description: Load a tiny Identity ONNX graph, print input/output names, run a 2x2 tensor
examples.learningGoal: Inspect a real ONNX graph without training one.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints identity input/output metadata, Y equals X, then onnx inspect ok.

examples.name: Dense layer helpers
examples.description: Train the XOR MLP with nn.dense and nn.denseBackward instead of hand-written chain-rule loops
examples.learningGoal: See the same 2-4-1 XOR net when the local derivative lives in nn.denseBackward.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints training loss and classifies all four XOR inputs, then nn dense ok.

examples.name: Sequential XOR
examples.description: Train the XOR MLP with new Sequential and Dense.fit instead of a handwritten step
examples.learningGoal: Define a 2-4-1 sigmoid stack and train it with online SGD in a few lines.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints the last-epoch loss and classifies all four XOR inputs, then sequential xor ok.

examples.name: Tiny digits (MNIST loop)
examples.description: Train a 5x5 glyph MLP with nn.dense, softmax cross-entropy, and a hand-written learning-rate step — the MNIST loop without the download
examples.learningGoal: Run the chapter 14 two-layer step on ten digit glyphs: ReLU hidden layer, linear logits, nn.softmaxGrad as upstream.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints training loss and classifies all ten glyphs, then mnist digits ok.

examples.name: REINFORCE bandit
examples.description: One-step policy gradient: a 1-4-2 net samples an action and scales nn.softmaxGrad by the return minus a baseline
examples.learningGoal: See nn.softmaxGrad of a sampled action, scaled by the return, raise the probability of the matching action.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints both action probabilities above 0.8 and a positive late return, then reinforce ok.

examples.name: Dense gradient check
examples.description: Compare nn.denseBackward to a central difference on each weight of one ReLU layer
examples.learningGoal: Trust nn.denseBackward by matching it to a numerical slope on every weight.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints a near-zero max gap, then gradcheck dense ok.

examples.name: Init scale
examples.description: One forward pass: uniform saturates, Xavier does not, He keeps ReLU activations smaller
examples.learningGoal: See why the scale of the random draw changes how many units saturate or explode.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints saturated and large-activation counts, then init scale ok.

examples.name: Glyph holdout
examples.description: Train the ten 5x5 glyphs, then score a copy with two flipped pixels that swaps 8 and 9
examples.learningGoal: See a net that classifies every clean glyph miss the same glyphs after two pixel flips.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints train accuracy 10/10 and a lower holdout accuracy, then glyph holdout ok.

examples.name: Momentum valley
examples.description: Plain SGD oscillates on a steep quadratic; momentum with a velocity walks down the valley
examples.learningGoal: See why one learning rate on a steep axis overshoots, and a velocity does not.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints a large SGD distance and a small momentum distance, then momentum valley ok.

examples.name: Gradient clip
examples.description: A steep quadratic step overshoots; capping the gradient length walks toward zero with the same learning rate
examples.learningGoal: See one learning rate explode on a steep gradient, and a length cap keep the same step small.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints a large unclipped magnitude and a clipped magnitude under 1, then grad clip ok.

examples.name: Adam valley
examples.description: Adam's bias-corrected moments walk the steep quadratic that plain SGD overshoots
examples.learningGoal: Update m and v yourself, then see Adam finish near the origin while SGD stays far.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints a large SGD distance and a small Adam distance, then adam valley ok.

examples.name: RNN delay
examples.description: A sigmoid recurrence shrinks its gradient, then a tanh Elman net recalls a bit from three steps ago
examples.learningGoal: See a product of sigmoid derivatives shrink, then train a short delay with an explicit backward pass.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints a shrinking recurrence gradient and delay recall, then rnn delay ok.

examples.name: Shared stroke kernel
examples.description: Slide one 3x3 kernel across 5x5 vertical and horizontal dashes and add every window into those nine weights
examples.learningGoal: See one kernel detect a stroke at several offsets because the backward pass reuses the same nine weights.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints full accuracy and a center column larger than the center row, then conv stroke ok.

examples.name: Residual and dropout
examples.description: A skip beats a deep sigmoid stack on y = x, then a Bernoulli mask zeros a unit only while training
examples.learningGoal: See a skip keep the identity that a deep sigmoid stack cannot fit, and a mask that eval does not apply.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints a lower residual loss, one masked activation, and eval zeros 0, then residual dropout ok.

examples.name: Embedding row
examples.description: One gradient step writes into the selected embedding row and leaves the other rows put
examples.learningGoal: See an embedding update as a table lookup whose gradient lands in one row.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints that row 0 moved and the other rows held, then embed row ok.

examples.name: Next character
examples.description: A bigram on a repeated word: embed the character, linear logits, scatter the gradient back into that row
examples.learningGoal: Train a one-step language model whose classifier gradient updates a single embedding row.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints a to b through f to a, then next char ok.

examples.name: Next character MLP
examples.description: Two characters of context: both samples end on a, and a ReLU hidden layer names b after x and c after y
examples.learningGoal: See a bigram fail when one character has two successors, and a two-row embedding plus a hidden layer name both.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints x a -> b and y a -> c, then next char mlp ok.

examples.name: Layer norm
examples.description: A deep matrix product grows; mean and standard deviation keep it near 1, and a central difference checks the scale
examples.learningGoal: See why a deep product needs a normalize step, and check the scale gradient by hand.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints a large plain peak, a small norm peak, and a near-zero gamma gap, then layer norm ok.

examples.name: Attention step
examples.description: One head: QK^T / sqrt(d), softmax, times V. Training attends to a marked token; a causal mask hides it
examples.learningGoal: Read one attention head as scores, softmax, and values, then see a causal mask block the future.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints a marker weight above 0.8 and a causal leak near 0, then attention step ok.

examples.name: Positional encoding
examples.description: Fixed sinusoidal positions: position 0 is sin 0 / cos 0, and position 1 matches sin(1) and cos(1)
examples.learningGoal: Read the 2017 position formula on its own, before it is added to a token vector.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints position 0 as 0 and 1, and a near-zero gap against sin(1) and cos(1), then positional encoding ok.

examples.name: Sentence decoder
examples.description: One causal attention block plus a linear readout overfits the next characters of abca
examples.learningGoal: Train one block — token plus sinusoid, causal head, residual, linear logits — until it reproduces bcab.
examples.expectedOutput: Prints abca -> bcab and 4/4, then sentence decoder ok.
